hero.title: Plan Technology and Integrations.
hero.intro: Turn requirements into component responsibilities, data flows and API contracts with reviewed trade-offs and failure plans.

fields.label: CEO architecture brief: requirement/spec version, core task, constraints, decision owner and resource boundary
Component responsibilities: interface, application/backend, data storage, external services; requirement IDs and build/buy/defer reasons
Data/action flow: source → component → destination, fields, purpose, permissions and retention unknowns
Technology alternatives: requirement fit, skills, operational effort/cost status, maintainability, portability/exit and evidence source
Integration/API contract: requirement link, method/path, request/response fields, access boundary and mock/sandbox/live status
Failure plan: timeout/denial/rate limit/invalid response, retry limits, safe fallback and duplicate-write prevention where relevant
Owner, budget/rate/time caps, environment separation, monitoring/log minimisation, capability reviews and revisit/stop triggers
Lesson 49 security/data input: architecture version, trust boundaries, data inventory, access/secret owners and unresolved risk decisions
Did tool familiarity or provider marketing override requirement fit, operating cost or exit needs?
Which simpler architecture or contradictory capability evidence could change this choice?
Which trust boundary, data/provider permission or unowned dependency blocks implementation?

sections.label: 01 / WATCH
sections.heading: Map the smallest system that can deliver the task.

scenes.title: Start with the product specification
scenes.narration: Architecture describes which parts do the work and how they interact. Begin with the scoped requirements from Lesson 47. The CEO decision is the smallest maintainable system that can meet the task and reviewed constraints.

scenes.title: Assign responsibilities
scenes.visual: Client, backend, data and provider diagram
scenes.narration: Separate the interface, application logic, storage and external services. A local prototype may not need a server yet. For real protected operations, explain the trust boundary and where authorization and secret credentials belong.

scenes.title: Map data and alternatives
scenes.narration: For each flow, name the data, purpose and destination. Compare build, buy or defer against capability, skills, operating effort, cost status and exit options. Do not invent prices, capacity or provider guarantees.

scenes.title: Define the API contract
scenes.narration: An API contract explains the operation and allowed inputs and outputs. Use requirement IDs, response types, access rules and environment status. Our fictional route contract returns ID, label and availability. The local exercise checks sample shape only and never calls a provider.

scenes.title: Plan failures and controls
scenes.narration: A system needs a safe path when a dependency fails. Define bounded retries, rate and time limits, and clear user recovery. For writes, consider duplicate effects and reconciliation. Record owners and unknowns before relying on an integration.

scenes.title: Review and hand off
scenes.visual: Versioned architecture brief to security/data checklist
scenes.narration: AI can draft component and contract options from supplied facts, but humans review the trade-offs and claims. Carry the architecture, data inventory, trust boundaries and unresolved decisions to Lesson 49 security and data principles. A diagram or sample check is not deployed architecture or security approval.

props.initial: Simulated guidance; field counts do not verify architecture.

children: Architect → integration reviewer → operations/cost reviewer → founder decision. Prepared prompts include your worksheet/register locally; inspect/redact before external sharing.

roles.architect: Propose minimal components, requirement links, responsibilities, data flows and build/buy/defer alternatives. Preserve capability, cost and source unknowns; do not prescribe unnecessary services.
roles.integration: Review supplied contracts for methods/paths, input/output schemas, access/environment status, timeout/denial/invalid-response handling, bounded retries and duplicate-write risks. Identify missing capability evidence; do not call providers or claim conformance.
roles.operations: Review owner/skills, operating effort and cost assumptions, caps, logging/data minimization, environments, portability/exit and revisit conditions. Do not invent prices, capacity, region or compliance guarantees.

prompt.middle:
